content.text:
Delivered: opted-out readers no longer get the newsletter when their address differs only in capitals or surrounding spaces. This fixes the Friday complaints.

**Cause:** `recipients()` normalized addresses to remove duplicates. It compared them to `optouts.csv` by exact string. An opt-out of `Jo.Bauer@example.org ` (capitals and a trailing space) did not match the subscriber `jo.bauer@example.org`. The README says these count as the same address.

**Fix:** `mailing.py` now normalizes the opt-out addresses (`opted_out`). `recipients()` compares the normalized subscriber address to them.

KB: No KB
Triggers: none fired.
Claims:
- Fulfilled: opt-outs match despite case and spaces. The new test `test_opt_out_matches_despite_case_and_spaces` failed before the fix and passes after it.
- Fulfilled: the four existing tests still pass. Full suite: 5 of 5 pass.
- Before the fix, three people were still on the list: `maria.k@example.net`, `Dev.Patel@Example.com` and `jo.bauer@example.org`. None of them is on it now.

Guesses: I treated "same address" as exactly the README rule (case and surrounding spaces). I did not handle other forms, such as `+tag` aliases or dots in Gmail addresses.
Disclosures: none.
Not checked: I did not run the real send job or the opt-out form. I only tested `recipients()`. I did not check whether the form can write other malformed rows.
To land: nothing needs your decision. The directory is not a git repository, so I did not commit anything. These three readers have already received mail they opted out of, so you may want to deal with that separately.
